cohort: The study included 59 pregnant women with COVID-19 infection who delivered after the third trimester, compared with 118 age-matched controls without infection, all from Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital Obstetrics Department.
finding: Pregnancy with COVID-19 infection was associated with significantly more adverse obstetric complications, higher rates of Cesarean section, and increased maternal ICU admission compared to pregnancies without infection, but no significant difference was observed in neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rates were significantly higher in women with COVID-19 infection (81.35%) compared to the control group (51.7%).
cross-section timing: Outcomes were measured around the time of delivery and immediate hospital stay.
birth_weight: Measured as an outcome, but specific weights not detailed in abstract.
gest_age: All participants delivered after the third trimester (i.e., > 28 weeks gestation).
